'''Derrick LeRon Williams''' (born May 25, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]] (BCL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] from 2009 to 2011. Williams was selected with the second overall pick by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. He spent two and a half seasons in Minnesota before being traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in November 2013. After two seasons with the Kings, Williams signed with the [[New York Knicks]] in July 2015. He later signed with the [[Miami Heat]] in July 2016 before being waived in February 2017. Williams joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] the same month, with whom he reached the [[2017 NBA Finals]]. He signed in China to start the 2017–18 season, but joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on a 10-day contract in March 2018. Williams has played overseas since October 2018. ==Early life== Williams was born in [[Bellflower, California]], and graduated from [[La Mirada High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willide02.html|title=Derrick Williams NBA Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 14, 2016}} ==College career== Williams originally committed to play at the University of Southern California.{{cite news| url=http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/sports_blog/2011/03/college-basketball-.html | work=Los Angeles Times | title=Sports Now}} He was quickly recruited by first-year head coach [[Sean Miller]] at the [[University of Arizona]]. ===Freshman year=== As a freshman in 2009–10, Williams averaged 15.7 points (7th in the Pac-10) and 7.1 rebounds per game, and had a field goal percentage of .575 (2nd in the Pac-10; 12th in the [[NCAA]]).{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/derrick-williams-2.html|title=Derrick Williams College Stats|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} He was named a freshman [[All-American]], [[All-Pac-12 men's basketball team|All-Pac-10]] first team and the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-10 Freshman of the Year]].[http://www.arizonawildcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033010aab.html Derrick Williams Named Freshman All-America] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307204724/http://www.arizonawildcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033010aab.html |date=March 7, 2012 }}. Arizonawildcats.com (March 30, 2010). Retrieved on 2012-07-09.Bryan Roy (March 8, 2010). [https://web.archive.org/web/20100314093154/http://wildcat.arizona.edu/sports/derrick-williams-wins-pac-10-freshman-of-year-1.1259362 Derrick Williams wins Pac-10 Freshman of Year]. Wildcat.arizona.edu. Retrieved on 2012-07-09. ===Sophomore year=== [[File:Derrick Williams of Arizona Wildcats.jpg|thumb|upright=0.75|Williams with [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] in 2011]] Williams rose to national prominence in his sophomore year. He averaged 19.5 points (2nd in the Pac-10) and 8.3 rebounds (4th) per game. During the 2011 season, Williams had a field goal percentage of .595 (tops in the Pac-10; 9th in the NCAA). He led the NCAA in True Shooting percentage (.690) and Effective Field Goal percentage (.650), helping lead the Arizona Wildcats basketball team to a regular season PAC-10 championship. Williams was named the Pac-10 Player of the Year.[http://www.azdesertswarm.com/2011/3/7/2035273/derrick-williams-named-pac-10-player-of-the-year-miller-earns-coy Arizona Daily Wildcat – Williams named Pac-10 Player of the Year]. Wildcat.arizona.edu (March 7, 2011). Retrieved on 2012-07-09. Williams also contributed to the Wildcats' run in the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. He made a critical block with less than 2 seconds against Memphis.[http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2011/mar/19/no-headline---2011-03-18-230954339423/ Tigers replay: Derrick Williams' block sealed Memphis' fate]. Commercialappeal.com (March 19, 2011). Retrieved on 2012-07-09. He had a 3-point play against the [[2010–11 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas Longhorns]], which advanced the Wildcats to the Sweet 16 of the tournament.[http://arizona.sbnation.com/arizona-wildcats/2011/3/19/2059100/arizona-vs-texas-sweet-16-ncaa-tournament--wildcats-longhorns Arizona vs. Texas: Wildcats Advance, Defeating Longhorns 70–69 – SB Nation Arizona]. Arizona.sbnation.com. Retrieved on July 9, 2012. Williams then had a career-high 32 points along with 13 rebounds to lead Arizona in an upset victory over the #1-seeded [[2010–11 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] by a 16-point margin to advance into the Elite Eight,{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2011-03-25-arizona-duke_N.htm | work=USA Today | title=Williams, Arizona trash defending champ Duke | date=March 25, 2011}} where they fell 65–63 to the future NCAA tournament champion, [[2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]].{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2011-03-26-connecticut-arizona_N.htm | work=USA Today | title=Walker gets help, UConn edges Arizona for spot in Final Four | date=March 27, 2011}} At the end of the season he was projected to be one of the top picks for the upcoming NBA draft.((espn.com)) Sophomore year honors: * [[Pac-10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Player of the Year]] * All-Pac-10 first team{{Cite web|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2011/03/07/2010-11-pac-10-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170221111453/http://pac-12.com/article/2011/03/07/2010-11-pac-10-conference-mens-basketball-honors|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 21, 2017|title=2010–11 Pac-10 Conference Men's Basketball Honors}} * Three time Pac-10 Player of the Week{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130117030836/http://www.arizonawildcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022111aag.html|title=Williams Named Pac-10 Player of the Week. On June 28, 2022, Williams officially parted ways with the Israeli club. === Panathinaikos (2022–2023) === On July 15, 2022, Williams signed a one-year contract with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |title=Williams Is "Green" |url=https://www.paobc.gr/en/press-releases/103175_williams-green |access-date=2022-07-16 |website=Panathinaikos BC |date=July 15, 2022 |language=en}} In 34 EuroLeague games, he averaged 12.4 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.2 assists, playing around 29 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 32 domestic league matches, he averaged 6.2 points and 2.1 rebounds, playing around 18 minutes per contest. On July 3, 2023, he was officially released from the team. === Mets de Guaynabo (2025) === Williams signed with the [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Guaynabo Mets]] to play under former teammate [[J. J. Barea|Jose Juan Barea]]. Through the early season (as of March 23, 2025), he averaged 14.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 0.3 steals per game over three games. Williams faced a setback with a $2,500 fine and a two-game suspension for disciplinary reasons following an incident on April 19, 2025, during a game against the [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] [https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/de-minnesota-al-bsn-jj-barea-y-derrick-williams-se-reencuentran-en-guaynabo/] === Suwon KT Sonicboom (2025–2026) === === AEK Athens (2026–present) === On August 17, 2026, Williams signed with [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] on a 1+1 contract.{{cite web |url=https://basketnews.com/news-253844-derrick-williams-returns-to-play-in-greece.html |title=Derrick Williams returns to play in Greece |website=BasketNews.com |date=August 17, 2026 |access-date=August 17, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#CFECEC;
